name: Etoricoxib
mechanism: Selective COX-2 inhibitor - reduces prostaglandin synthesis while sparing COX-1 (less GI toxicity)
dosing: Osteoarthritis: 30mg OD. Rheumatoid arthritis/ankylosing spondylitis: 60mg OD. Acute gout: 120mg OD for max 8 days
contraindications: Active peptic ulcer, inflammatory bowel disease, heart failure, ischaemic heart disease, stroke, peripheral arterial disease, uncontrolled hypertension
interactions: Warfarin (↑ INR), ACE inhibitors (↓ effect, ↑ nephrotoxicity), diuretics (↓ effect), lithium (↑ levels)
monitoring: Blood pressure, renal function, cardiovascular risk factors, signs of GI bleeding
pregnancy: Avoid - may cause premature closure of ductus arteriosus, delay labour. Contraindicated in 3rd trimester
sideEffects: Hypertension, oedema, GI disturbance, headache, dizziness, increased cardiovascular risk, renal impairment
pharmacokinetics: Good oral absorption, 100% bioavailability, highly protein bound (92%), half-life: 22 hours, hepatic metabolism
clinicalPearls: Lower GI bleeding risk than non-selective NSAIDs but higher cardiovascular risk. Use lowest effective dose for shortest duration. Check BP within 2 weeks of starting
indication: Osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, acute gout
